step1.title: Your notebook. Not hers.
step1.body: HerDay helps you understand her menstrual cycle — where she is, what it changes for her — and be there at the right moment. She’ll never get a notification or be asked to log anything.
step1.body2: HerDay helps you become a proactive partner, not a reactive one: stop asking, start understanding and acting.
step1.email_hint: We send you a magic link. No password.

step2.title: You do it to help her, not behind her back.
step2.body1: HerDay is your notebook. It sends nothing to your partner. It appears in no notification on her end.
step2.body2: But we strongly recommend you tell her about it, and even show it to her. Why: an observation tool used in silence ends up replacing the conversation instead of nourishing it. That's the opposite of what we want here.
step2.choice_soon: I'll tell her about it soon
step2.choice_already: I've already told her about it
step2.change_later: You can change your answer at any time in the settings.

step3.title: Her cycle, like a day.
step3.body: Four moments that come back every month. Tap them to discover them.
step3.more_info: Based on the medical literature. Each phase in detail, and the sources, are in the app.

step_obs.title: You observe, the app remembers.
step_obs.obs_body: Every day, in a few seconds: a pill, what helped, what didn’t. Your notes go into your journal — nobody else reads it.
step_obs.echo_body: When the same moment of the cycle comes back, your notes return as echoes: repeat what works, avoid what doesn’t.

step4.title: When did her last period start, as far as you know?
step4.body: Imprecision is normal and invalidates nothing. You can correct it at any time.
step4.length_hint: Low confidence score until you're sure. That's healthy.
step4.unknown_hint: No problem: you explore the app without a forecast. As soon as her period comes, a button on the home screen lets you log it, and tracking starts.
step4.contraception_hint: The pill, implant, ring… often block ovulation: the phases don’t apply the same way. The app will remind you.
step4.confidence_body: It tells how reliable the forecast is. Low at first, it rises once you confirm two period starts.

step_partner.title: How well do you know the menstrual cycle?
step_partner.body: No wrong answer: it only sets how much the app explains.
step_partner.nickname_hint: A first name or a nickname, only for the app’s sentences. Leave empty to keep the pronoun.

decouverte.title: I’m new to this
decouverte.body: We explain everything, simply, day by day.

bases.title: I know the basics
bases.body: Period, ovulation: got it. The rest, less so.

nuit.body: Energy drops, then the period comes: tiredness, possible pain, a need for calm.

aube.body: Recovery. Energy slowly comes back, mood lifts.

jour.body: Peak energy and confidence. The right time for plans and outings together.

crepuscule.body: Steady energy, a wish for concrete things and refocusing.

step_tools.title: Keep an eye on it, discreetly.
step_tools.agenda_body: Subscribe your calendar (Google, Apple, Outlook) from the settings: two neutral markers, “Period A” and “Period B”.
step_tools.widget_body: The dial on your home screen: long press, “+”, then HerDay.
step_tools.later: You can do all this later, in the settings.
